field: evidence[].doi — publisher internal article ID confusion
observation: 'jmai-24-10776' is not a second DOI or an alternate/competing identifier for a different paper — it is AME Publishing's internal manuscript/article slug for the SAME article (URL https://jmai.amegroups.org/article/view/10776/html), assigned when the paper was received in 2024 (hence the '24' prefix) and later published with DOI suffix 'jmai-2025-173' reflecting the 2025 acceptance/publication-year numbering convention AME uses. suggested_fix: Keep DOI as 10.21037/jmai-2025-173 (Crossref-registered, resolves, metadata matches). Do not substitute jmai-24-10776; it is only a publisher URL slug, not a citable DOI.

suggested_fix: Add this DOI as a rigor/impact source or at minimum a qualityFlag/limitation noting structure-definition discordance for esophagus and spinal canal; do not let the paper's favorable 5-OAR performance (DSC 0.92) overshadow the 2-OAR divergence in any impact rationale.

observation: Current impactSource (Vaassen 2020) is explicitly flagged vendorIndependent:false and prototype-stage, which is already transparently disclosed — correctly not marked 'clean'.

observation: The same DOI (10.1016/j.phro.2026.100999) is used for BOTH rigorSource and impactSource, which is internally consistent but means the E2/L4 rating rests on a single prospective single-centre study rather than independent corroboration. A second relevant paper exists (Barati/Duan et al., regression-test study of a commercial RayStation DLS model, acm2.70824) that could diversify the evidence base.
suggested_fix: Consider adding the regression-test study as a secondary rigor/impact source, or note in qualityFlags that evidence currently relies on a single study/DOI for both scores.

observation: impactSource rationale names 'ART-Plan' (Therapanacea's umbrella platform) for a real-world H&N evaluation, but Annotate is the contouring module within ART-Plan, not a separately branded product in the cited study. This is a brand-granularity issue: product-level attribution (Annotate) vs. platform-level attribution (ART-Plan) is blurred.
suggested_fix: Clarify in rationale whether the paper tested the Annotate module specifically or the ART-Plan platform broadly, since both Annotate and SmartPlan are marketed as separate modules of ART-Plan.

observation: static-audit.json correctly shows rigor E0 / impact L1c (stored, provisional, paperCount 0, vendorIndependent:false) for TumorBox — no inflated or falsely-clean scoring found; vendor marketing states '93% time saved' but this is explicitly NOT reflected in the independently computed score.
suggested_fix: None; this is an example of appropriately conservative (non-'clean') scoring that should be preserved.

observation: Vendor's own US site lists BrachyBox under 'Coming Soon' (not yet released) as of the search snapshot, while static-audit.json already shows E0/L2 stored/provisional with paperCount 0 — consistent, not falsely 'clean'.
suggested_fix: Confirm current release status before any future score upgrade; flag product as pre-release in public-facing records if still accurate.

observation: Jazz is described on the vendor's own site as a neuroradiology 'lesion tracking and reporting' tool for diagnostic MS follow-up (single-click annotation, volumetric lesion tracking, automated report generation) — it is not a radiotherapy organ/target auto-contouring product. Its sole supporting publication (Federau et al., Neuroradiology 2024) evaluates diagnostic MS-lesion reading productivity/quality, not RT contouring. Classifying Jazz under 'Auto-Contouring' (an RT category) alongside true OAR/target contouring tools like Limbus or MVision is a category-fit mismatch.
suggested_fix: Re-examine whether Jazz belongs in the Auto-Contouring (radiotherapy) category at all, or whether it should be reclassified/footnoted as a diagnostic neuroradiology tool with only tangential RT relevance. At minimum, the impact rationale should state explicitly that the supporting evidence is diagnostic, not RT-contouring, evidence.

observation: L3 clinical impact label for Jazz is derived from a diagnostic-radiology productivity study, not a radiotherapy planning/dosimetric study — applying an RT clinical-impact tier to non-RT evidence risks a false 'clean' L3 impact rating.
suggested_fix: Down-grade or re-derive the impact label using RT-specific criteria, or mark impact as not-applicable/out-of-scope for RT auto-contouring comparisons.

observation: publication-checks.json requestedTitle for key 10.1002/mp.16299 is 'Follow-up evaluation of IntContour', but the actual paper (Duan, Bernard, Castle, Feng, Wang, Kenamond, Chen, Med Phys 2023) is 'Contouring quality assurance methodology based on multiple geometric features against deep learning auto-segmentation' — a generic DLAS-based manual-contour QA classifier study using a public 339-case dataset, not a clinical evaluation of the IntContour product itself. Two co-authors (Castle, Feng) are listed as affiliated with 'Carina Medical LLC' per the University of Kentucky repository record, so the paper has an undisclosed vendor-affiliation link to Carina AI, but it is not a 'follow-up evaluation of IntContour' as the requested title implies.
suggested_fix: Correct the requestedTitle/attribution to the paper's actual title and scope (a generic QA-classifier methodology study with Carina-affiliated co-authors), and flag vendorIndependent:false rather than implying it is an independent or product-specific follow-up validation.

observation: Both rigorSource and impactSource use the identical DOI (10.1016/j.ijrobp.2024.02.041) and both are breast-only; AVIEW RT-ACS has several other vendor-published breast studies (2020, 2021 IJROBP/Radiat Oncol) that could broaden the evidence base but all are also breast-specific and largely vendor-coauthored.
suggested_fix: Note in limitations/qualityFlags that AVIEW RT-ACS's clinical evidence to date is concentrated in a single anatomical site (breast) and largely authored by groups with repeat vendor collaboration (Coreline-affiliated co-authors across multiple cited studies).

observation: static-audit.json correctly scores RT Suite v1 as E0/L1c stored/provisional with paperCount 0 — no clinical paper is directly tied to this product in the scoring, which is accurate since the one identified EFAI-related paper (radonc.2023.109528) is attached to Seg Pro V3's record instead, not RT Suite's.

observation: static-audit.json rationale for Seg Pro V3 is self-disclosed as evaluating 'the shared EFAI segmentation engine rather than the Seg Pro V3 release specifically' with vendorIndependent:false — this is already correctly flagged as non-clean/non-independent, consistent with the FDA record showing Seg Pro V3 (RT-300, K251306) is a later, distinct 510(k) clearance from the original EFAI RTSUITE (K231928) used in the 2023 paper.
suggested_fix: None required beyond what is already disclosed; confirm in any future product-page copy that Seg Pro V3 and the cited 2023 paper's software version are not conflated as identical products.

observation: rigorOrigin/impactOrigin are 'stored' (not 'papers') with paperCount 1 but scoredPaperCount 0, meaning the E1/L3 rating is not derived from a scored literature entry yet qualityFlags report multiCenter:true, multiNational:true and externalValidation:true as if already substantiated — a potential false 'clean' quality-flag state given no scored paper backs the claim.
suggested_fix: Either attach the specific paperCount=1 source explicitly so its multi-center/multi-national/external-validation claims can be verified, or set these qualityFlags to false/unknown until a scorable source is linked.

observation: static-audit.json correctly scores DV.TARGET E0/L1c, stored/provisional, paperCount 0, vendorIndependent:false — consistent with the FDA 510(k) summary (K202928) showing only a single-site (City of Hope) retrospective comparison study, no independent peer-reviewed clinical publication identified.
suggested_fix: None — conservative scoring correctly avoids a false 'clean' rating despite vendor-listed publications (Tang 2019, Zhu 2019, Sun 2020) that describe the underlying algorithm research rather than the commercial DV.TARGET product in clinical use.

observation: publication-checks.json requestedTitle for 10.3389/fonc.2022.833816 is 'AccuContour clinical evaluation' vs. actual title 'Evaluation Exploration of Atlas-Based and Deep Learning-Based Automatic Contouring for Nasopharyngeal Carcinoma.' Unlike the IntContour case, the abstract DOES confirm AccuContour® is the DL-based model used, and two co-authors (Chen, Yang) are Manteia Technologies employees. The requestedTitle is a paraphrase/shorthand, not a false attribution — product and vendor-affiliation are both correctly identifiable from the real title/abstract.
suggested_fix: Low-priority: replace the paraphrased requestedTitle with the verbatim published title to avoid any appearance of a mismatch, but no substantive correction needed.

observation: Current rigorSource (Zhu et al. 2025, phro.2025.100886) is vendor-independent per qualityFlags, but a more recent, more directly relevant Manteia-coauthored paper exists (Yan/Fei et al., Sci Rep 2025, 'Consistency evaluation and performance optimization of deep learning-based auto-contouring for nasopharyngeal carcinoma') with Manteia Technologies co-authors — not currently reflected in the scored evidence set.
suggested_fix: Consider adding the 2025 Scientific Reports paper as an additional (vendor-affiliated) evidence point, clearly flagged vendorIndependent:false.

observation: static-audit.json lists the journal for DOI 10.1186/s13014-024-02451-4 as 'Radiother Oncol' (Elsevier's Radiotherapy and Oncology). The actual journal is 'Radiation Oncology' (BioMed Central/Springer open-access journal, ISSN 1748-717X, PMC-indexed as 'Radiat Oncol'), a distinct journal from Elsevier's Radiotherapy and Oncology. This is a confirmed journal-identity mismatch.
suggested_fix: Correct journal field to 'Radiation Oncology' (BMC) across all records citing this DOI.

observation: static-audit.json title/rationale for this DOI reads 'Multi-vendor auto-contouring comparison across 5 facilities' and 'Multi-centre evaluation across five facilities including review and edit effort,' with multiCenter:true in both score and qualityFlags. The actual paper (Goddard et al. 2024) is a SINGLE-institution study: all nine authors are affiliated with Montefiore Medical Center / Albert Einstein College of Medicine, using one Siemens-SOMATOMgo scanner and 47 patients — there is no mention of '5 facilities' anywhere in the title, abstract, or author affiliations. This fabricated 'five facilities' / 'multi-centre' claim inflates both the evidentiary rigor (contributing to the E2 rating) and the multiCenter/externalValidation quality flags for mim-contour-protegeai.
suggested_fix: Correct title field to 'Evaluation of multiple-vendor AI autocontouring solutions', remove the fabricated '5 facilities'/multi-centre framing from the rationale, set multiCenter:false in both score.rigorSource and qualityFlags, and re-assess whether E2 rigor is still warranted for a single-institution, single-scanner, 47-patient study (likely should drop toward E1 unless other corroborating multi-site evidence is added).

observation: Top-level qualityFlags.multiCenter:true for mim-contour-protegeai is a false 'clean' flag directly caused by the fabricated '5 facilities' claim above; this flag should not be marked true/passing.
suggested_fix: Set qualityFlags.multiCenter to false and re-derive computedRigor accordingly.

observation: Identical journal-name error as mim-contour-protegeai: 'Radiother Oncol' listed instead of the correct 'Radiation Oncology' (BMC) for DOI 10.1186/s13014-024-02451-4.

observation: Same fabricated claim as mim-contour-protegeai: requestedTitle/rationale state 'Auto-contouring comparison across 5 facilities including Radformation' and 'Multi-centre evaluation across five facilities,' with multiCenter:true — but Goddard et al. 2024 is a single-institution (Montefiore/Einstein), single-scanner, 47-patient study. suggested_fix: Correct title to 'Evaluation of multiple-vendor AI autocontouring solutions', remove 'five facilities'/multi-centre language, set multiCenter:false, and re-assess E2 rigor rating given the smaller single-site evidence base.
